correctness.rationale: Every nontrivial positive solution is reversibly reduced to \(r>1\) and then to \(s>0\). The derived formulas for \(z\), \(t\), and \(\lambda\) substitute back exactly. Strict convexity of \(u\coth(us)\) makes \(\log\lambda(s)\) strictly decreasing, while endpoint limits give a bijection onto the subcritical activity interval. The unique fixed point supplies the third solution. Taylor expansion gives the merger law. The proof is all-order; finite replay checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The source itself leaves the arbitrary-order \(I_2\) conclusion at “at least three,” while giving exact counts only in the first two orders. Closing that gap gives a natural complete branch classification for every \(k\ge2\), a unique global parameterization of the symmetry-broken pair, and its critical onset. This is not an arbitrary slice or a numerical refinement; it converts an existence theorem on a source-designated invariant branch into an exact global count.
